marks.gloss_en: תניא כוותיה דרבי אמי בר טביומי: remnants of a shifa/gemi mat, though below its measure, are not used for roofing
a mat of shifa or of gemi -- its remnants, though reduced below its measure, one does not roof with them
R' Eliezer: a bed becomes impure as a whole and becomes pure as a whole
for what is it fit? to lean them against a wall and sit on them, and to lay ropes across
what are worn-out vessels? Abaye: rags that do not have three by three [fingerbreadths], which are fit neither for the poor nor for the rich
a reed mat: a large one -- one roofs with it
תניא נמי הכי: הרי זו סוכה. והאנן תנן אינה סוכה! אלא לאו שמע מינה כדרב הונא. שמע מינה -- against the mishnah, the baraita must speak of a case with the space
the baraita: one who hollows out a grain stack to make himself a sukkah -- it is a sukkah
תנן: החוטט בגדיש לעשות לו סוכה אינה סוכה; והא תניא: הרי זו סוכה!
לא קשיא: כאן בשיש שם חלל טפח במשך שבעה, כאן בשאין שם חלל טפח במשך שבעה
Rav Huna (איכא דרמי): here (the baraita) -- where there is a space of a handbreadth along seven
the mishnah: one who hollows out a grain stack to make himself a sukkah -- it is not a sukkah
one who lowers walls from above downward: if [the wall] is three tefachim above the ground, [the sukkah] is invalid
the stam: the mishnah's dispute turns on whether a suspended partition permits
a cistern between two courtyards: one may not draw from it on Shabbat unless he made it a partition of ten tefachim, whether above, below, or within its rim
